findings.statement: the browser reader is under a 64 KB gzipped budget
findings.detail: 36170 bytes gzipped (76836 raw) against a budget of 65536. Hand-written C ABI rather than a binding generator, opt-level z, fat LTO, panic=abort, stripped

findings.statement: most of the module is supdb rather than the Rust runtime it is built on
findings.detail: an empty cdylib with the same standard-library surface is 12670 bytes gzipped (26701 raw), so supdb's marginal cost is 23500 gzipped (50135 raw) and the floor is 35% of what ships. The floor is not reducible from this side: it is the allocator, the panic machinery and `core::fmt`, which `std::io::Error` pulls in whatever it is reporting

findings.statement: supdb's own contribution to the bundle is under 32 KB gzipped
findings.detail: 23500 bytes gzipped above the floor, against 32768. This is the number that moves when the reader grows; W3.1 is the one the user pays
